speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To begin my assessment, how would you describe the onset of your fatigue and swelling—was it sudden or gradual? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your urine output or color?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty breathing, particularly when lying flat, or have you noticed any pain or blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Serum Albumin, Creatinine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein 4+, Blood Negative, Glucose Negative, WBC 0–1/hpf, Fatty_casts Numerous; Serum Albumin: 1.8 mg/dL; Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have Lower leg swelling, Unintentional weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Chronic bronchitis. Social history: History of smoking one pack of cigarettes daily for 44 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage daily.

speaker: Patient
text: The patient denies any recent cough, change in urinary habits, chest pain, dyspnea, or fevers. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrotic Syndrome (likely membranous nephropathy given age and weight loss).
